novelty_basis: A small exhaustive census; termination of one-rule systems is a classical topic (Zantema-Geser, Dershowitz "Open. Closed. Open.", RTA 2005) and this observation is likely folklore.
proof_check: computer-assisted (Python) - explicit termination certificates (length decrease, lexicographic monotonicity, linear interpretations over N, decreasing factor counts) for 162 rules and self-embeddings for 34, all re-checked independently
statement:
Among the 196 rules l -> r over {a,b} with 1 <= |l| <= 3, 0 <= |r| <= 3, l != r, exactly the 34 rules in
which l is a factor of r are non-terminating; the other 162 terminate.
title: Termination census of one-rule systems with |l|, |r| <= 3: non-terminating iff l is a factor of r
